# Final comparison — what this project established

**Task:** T4.4 · **Generated by:** `scripts/final_comparison.py`

> POSITIVE CLASS = Attack (label 1); negative class = Normal (label 0). This is TRD.md §2.3's convention and is the OPPOSITE of the base paper's, which uses Normal as positive (PRD.md §2.1.3).

Numbers are read from the generated result tables, not transcribed, so this document
cannot drift from the measurements it summarises.

---

## 1. The four objections, and what came of each

| # | Objection to HIDS-IoMT | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Pre-split SMOTE inflates the headline number | **Confirmed, and fixed** | `notebooks/01_reproduce_leakage.ipynb`, `02_leakage_free_baseline.ipynb` |
| 2 | The LSTM is never specified; input is a single record | **Fixed** | `docs/architecture_decision.md`, `reports/phase2_results.md` §2 |
| 3 | Precision and recall labels are swapped | **Confirmed by re-derivation** | `PRD.md §10`; every table in this repo states its positive class |
| 4 | Black box, flat 500 ms threshold for every device | **Partly fixed** | `reports/t3_3_xai_evaluation.md`, `reports/t3_4_adaptive_threshold.md` |

### Objection 1 — confirmed more strongly than the PRD claimed

IoTID20's cleaned majority class is 585,342 rows, and 2 x 585,342 = **1,170,684**, which
reproduces the base paper's stated post-SMOTE total **exactly**. Its train/test/validation
totals therefore partition synthetic data. Reproducing that pipeline order put **46.61%**
of the test fold into rows that never existed in the real capture, and 93.21% of its
minority-class rows.

One correction in the other direction, recorded because this project does not get to round
in its own favour: `PRD.md §2.1.1` says the paper's split totals match its post-SMOTE count
"exactly". They sum to 1,170,686 — **two more**. Trivial, and it does not weaken the
objection, but the PRD's wording should read "within 2 rows of".

### An additional defect this project found

**58.2% of cleaned IoTID20 rows are exact duplicates.** Random splitting puts identical
records on both sides regardless of when SMOTE runs, and neither the base paper nor the
senior's prior work mentions deduplication. Fixing the SMOTE ordering alone did **not**
lower the accuracy; the duplicates were the larger leakage vector.

## 2. This project's own numbers

### 2.1 Establishing an honest baseline

| Pipeline | Accuracy | Precision | Recall | F1 | Test fold synthetic | Near-duplicate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A. Leaky (base paper's order) | 0.9986 | 0.9975 | 0.9996 | 0.9986 | 46.61% | 43.98% |
| **C. Leakage-free + deduplicated** | **0.9964** | **0.9971** | **0.9990** | **0.9980** | **0.00%** | **5.70%** |

Pipeline C is this project's baseline. It is a Random Forest on individual flow records.

### 2.2 The ensemble

| Model | Accuracy | Precision | Recall | F1 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **transformer alone** | 0.9487 | 0.9678 | 0.9735 | **0.9707** |
| Full three-branch ensemble | 0.9399 | 0.9497 | 0.9831 | 0.9661 |

**The best single branch beats the ensemble** (0.9707 vs 0.9661). Both candidate fixes — per-branch calibration and fitted fusion priors
— were measured and both failed (`docs/calibration_decision.md`). The branches agree on
90.9% of windows, so any fusion rule has a ceiling of +0.026 accuracy over the best branch.

**These numbers are not comparable to §2.1's.** The baseline classifies flow *records*;
the ensemble classifies 10-record *windows*, on session-level folds, with class weights
rather than SMOTE. Three variables differ, so the difference is not attributable to
architecture (`reports/phase2_results.md` §5).

## 3. Against the base paper

HIDS-IoMT reports 99.92% accuracy, 99.91% precision, 99.99% recall, and 99.95% F1 on IoTID20. **These figures carry two defects and must never be quoted without them.** First, the precision and recall labels are very likely *swapped*: the paper defines its positive class as *Normal* and labels both Equations 7 and 8 "Recall", one of which is the precision formula. Recomputing from its own Fig. 11c confusion matrix (87,987 / 77 / 9 / 28,996) reproduces the reported accuracy exactly but shows the reported "precision" (99.913%) is the true recall and the reported "recall" (99.99%) is the true precision (`PRD.md §10`). Second, the evaluation fold was contaminated: the paper's post-SMOTE instance count of 1,170,684 is reproduced *exactly* by balancing IoTID20's cleaned majority class (2 x 585,342), so its train/test/validation folds partition synthetic data — reproduced empirically in `notebooks/01_reproduce_leakage.ipynb`, where 46.61% of the resulting test fold never existed in the real capture.

**No comparison of this project's numbers against those is offered, because none would be
meaningful.** A number produced on a contaminated evaluation fold and a number produced on
a clean one do not measure the same thing, and placing them in a table side by side would
imply otherwise. `PRD.md §5.3` puts beating that figure explicitly out of scope, and
`PRD.md §3` defines success as fixing the four defects rather than exceeding a disputed
value.

What can be said: this project's leakage-free baseline reaches **0.9980 F1** on a test fold that is 0.00% synthetic, with the positive
class stated and every metric hand-verified against its confusion matrix.

## 4. Against the senior's prior work

`PRD.md §2.2` lists five gaps in the Badiyani stacking ensemble. Four are addressed:

| Gap | Addressed? |
|---|---|
| Wrong domain (CICIDS2017, no IoMT traffic) | Yes — IoTID20 throughout |
| No temporal modelling | Yes — 10-record sequences, BiLSTM and attention branches |
| No deployment evidence despite a real-time claim | **Partly** — the export is built and verified, but no Pi measurement exists (§6) |
| IQR outlier removal deletes rare attacks | Yes — no outlier removal in this pipeline |
| No repeated runs or significance testing | **No** — this project inherits the same gap (§5) |

## 5. What this project did not establish

Listed because a comparison that reports only its wins is the failure mode this whole
project was built to criticise.

1. **The ensemble does not beat its best single branch on IoTID20.** Reported in full in
   `reports/ablation_study.md`, including that removing the CNN *improves* the ensemble.
2. **`PRD.md §3`'s >30% false-positive reduction target was not met.** The best measured
   reduction is −10.8%, and the criticality labels driving it are synthetic because IoTID20
   contains no medical devices (`reports/t3_4_adaptive_threshold.md`).
3. **No Raspberry Pi latency or throughput number exists.** The hardware is not available;
   the code refuses to emit one off-device (§6).
4. **Edge-IIoTset (T3.6) was not run**, so every conclusion here is IoTID20-only.
5. **Single seed, single split, no significance testing** — the same omission this project
   criticises in the prior work.
6. **T3.3's human readability gate is open.** The quantitative XAI metrics pass, but the
   reader test in `reports/t3_3_reader_test.md` needs a person to complete it.
7. **LIME proved unusable** as an operator-facing explainer: 0.27 top-5 Jaccard under 1%
   input noise, and no statistically significant fidelity at any k
   (`reports/t3_3_xai_evaluation.md`).

## 6. Deployment status

The inference graph is exported, verified, and bundled: three TFLite models totalling
1.4 MB (798 KB at float16), reproducing the evaluated ensemble's predictions with **100%**
agreement, plus a standalone runner that imports nothing from this repository
(`reports/t4_1_export.md`, `docs/raspberry_pi_setup.md`).

**No latency or throughput figure appears anywhere in this repository**, because the
Raspberry Pi 4B has not been connected. `src/deployment/benchmark.py` raises
`NotOnTargetHardwareError` rather than writing a report off-device. `PRD.md §2.2`'s
objection to the prior work is a real-time claim with no hardware behind it, and the
prohibition is enforced in code rather than left to discipline.

## 7. What this project actually contributes

1. **A reproducible demonstration that HIDS-IoMT's evaluation fold was contaminated**, with
   the arithmetic matching its own published totals exactly.
2. **A re-derivation showing its precision and recall labels are swapped**, from its own
   confusion matrix.
3. **A previously unreported defect in IoTID20's use across this literature**: 58.2%
   duplicate rows, a larger leakage vector than the SMOTE ordering.
4. **A fully specified sequence architecture** — every layer, unit, head and window count
   documented in code and asserted by test. The direct fix for Objection #2.
5. **Measured evidence that IoTID20's IP-pair graph cannot support a GNN** (99.68% of nodes
   have degree ≤ 1) — worth stating for anyone proposing graph-based IDS on flow records.
6. **An explainability layer that certifies each explanation before showing it**, and
   labels the 18% it cannot vouch for rather than hiding them.
7. **A set of negative results**: the ensemble does not beat its best branch, calibration
   does not help, fitted fusion priors overfit, and LIME is too unstable to show an
   operator. Each is measured, reproducible, and reported.
